strategies.summary: Run the entire SqueezeNet forward pass under torch.autocast(float16). At batch=64 and 512x512 inputs the dominant cost is memory bandwidth across the large early feature maps and the many Fire-module convolutions. fp16 halves the bandwidth pressure and unlocks tensor-core throughput on all the1x1 and 3x3 convolutions. Cast output back to float32 before returning to satisfy correctness checks.
implementation_hints: In init_body call self.features.half() and self.classifier.half() so weights are fp16 from the start; keep channels_last and cudnn.benchmark.
In forward_stmt_1 convert the input: x = x.half().contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last) if x.is_cuda else x.half().
Wrap forward_stmt_2 and forward_stmt_3 inside with torch.autocast(device_type='cuda', dtype=torch.float16): to guarantee autocast scope covers all layers.
In forward_stmt_4 cast the flattened output back to float32: return torch.flatten(x, 1).float() to match the reference dtype.
Do not change cuda_cpp or cuda_cu; this is a pure Python-path change.
Keep the existing torch.channels_last path intact; NHWC and fp16 compose correctly with cuDNN.
strategies.expected_gain: 30â50% wall-time reduction on Ampere/Turing GPUs due to halved memory traffic and tensor-core utilisation on all Fire-module convolutions.
risk_notes: Output must be cast back to float32 before return or correctness checks against the fp32 reference will fail.

Numerical tolerance: torch.allclose with default rtol=1e-5 will fail after fp16 round-trips; the benchmark typically uses atol=1e-2 for inference tasksâverify tolerance settings before relying on this.
Some BatchNorm-like ops accumulate in fp32 even under autocast;SqueezeNet has no BN so this is not a concern.
Channels-last and fp16 together require cuDNN >= 8.0; this is satisfied on any modern CUDA 11+ environment.
forbidden_patterns: Do not return a float16 tensor; always cast to float32 at the end.
Do not call .float() on intermediate activations inside the forward; let autocast manage upcasting.
Do not remove torch.channels_last from the input conversion path.

review_notes.openai-compatible: High upside on conv-heavy SqueezeNet and easy to implement, but full-model fp16/autocast can fail strict accuracy checks and forcing module weights to half raises correctness risk versus using autocast alone.
review_notes.claude-compatible: High confidence, low risk. fp16 autocast is well-understood, directly addresses the dominant memory bandwidth bottleneck across SqueezeNet's many small convolutions, and composes cleanly with the existing channels-last path. The only real risk is the output dtype cast, which is explicitly handled. Straightforward to implement correctly.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Autocast to FP16 is a standard and highly effective optimization for inference, though it carries a slight risk of failing strict numerical tolerance checks depending on the benchmark harness.

strategies.summary: Replace the classifier sequence (Conv2d 512â1000, ReLU, AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1,1)) with a single fused CUDA kernel. The 1x1 convolution is mathematically a per-pixel dot-product; the kernel can accumulate the weighted sum directly across all HÃW positions, apply ReLU to the accumulated value, and write only the [N, num_classes] output. This avoids materialising the large intermediate [64, 1000, H_cls, H_cls] tensor (~237 MB at spatial31Ã31) which is the dominant bandwidth cost of the classifier stage.
implementation_hints: Export one function from cuda_cpp: fused_conv1x1_relu_mean(torch::Tensor input, torch::Tensor weight, torch::Tensor bias) -> torch::Tensor returning shape [N, C_out].

In cuda_cu: launch a2-D grid where grid.x = N*C_out blocks and each block reduces over C_in * H * W. Use shared memory for partial sums; with 1x1 kernel the reduction per output is sum_over_c_in_and_spatial(weight[c_out, c_in] * input[n, c_in, h, w]) / (H*W) then relu.
A practical tile: one block handles one (n, c_out) pair; threads each take a stride over (c_in, h, w) and accumulate into shared memory, then do a warp-level reduce.

Access weight as [C_out, C_in] (NCHW weight layout, already correct for 1x1 conv) and input as [N, C_in, H, W] contiguous channels-last â ensure input is made contiguous(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format) before passing to the kernel.
